summary: Both hypotheses confirmed: Pósa rotation with Warnsdorff greedy scored 72/100, beating the greedy-only control at 41/100 by 31 points. The rotation mechanism is decisive on medium graphs (n=1K–8K) where it converts partial coverage into full Hamiltonian paths on 7/10 tests, but fails on 3 hard tests with sparse/low-degree structures (tests 4, 8, 10 scoring 1/10, 1/10, 0/10 respectively).
key_points: h-main (Pósa rotations): predicted ≥50, observed 72 — CONFIRMED. Achieves full Hamiltonian path on 7/10 tests (70 points from those), with partial credit of 1 each on tests 4 and 8.
h-control-negative (greedy only): predicted 35–45, observed 41 — CONFIRMED. Gets stuck at 56–84% vertex coverage on medium graphs, only solves the 3 smallest tests perfectly.

The 31-point gap is entirely from tests 5–7 and 9 (medium graphs, n=1K–8K, avg degree ≥5.4), where rotations escape dead ends and find the full Hamiltonian path (10/10 each) while greedy alone scores only 2–3/10.

Remaining 28 points are lost on 3 hard tests: test 4 (n=500, k=223, score 1/10), test 8 (n=9000, k=3309, score 1/10), test 10 (n=100K, k=4966, score 0/10) — all have high proportions of low-degree vertices (16–41%) making rotation ineffective.

Next iteration should target the 3 failing tests with stronger techniques: DFS backtracking for small test 4 (n=500), multi-restart or simulated annealing for test 8, and a scalable heuristic (e.g., Lin-Kernighan style or SCC-based ordering) for the large test 10 (n=100K).
